task_completion.description: The OpenBCI GUI is open and active on the screen.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The OpenBCI GUI window is visible, showing the EEG visualization interface.

task_completion.description: A Synthetic EEG session is currently running.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Start Data Stream' button is active or the EEG waveforms are actively scrolling across the screen, with the data source indicated as 'Synthetic'.

task_completion.description: The agent navigates to the Settings menu to find Expert Mode.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Settings' dropdown menu is clicked and visible in the top navigation bar.

task_completion.description: Expert Mode is toggled to 'On' within the interface.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Expert Mode' toggle or button in the Settings menu is shown in the 'On' state, or a visual indicator (like a label or color change) confirms Expert Mode is active.

task_completion.description: The agent uses the 'm' keyboard shortcut to trigger a screenshot.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A notification or console message appears in the GUI indicating a screenshot has been saved to '~/Documents/OpenBCI_GUI/Screenshots/', or the agent is seen typing 'm' while the GUI is in focus.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the GUI elements rather than using terminal commands to modify config files.
integrity.visual_evidence: The mouse cursor is seen clicking the Settings menu and the Expert Mode toggle; no terminal window is used to bypass the UI.

integrity.description: The screenshot was generated by the software's internal function, not by an OS-level print-screen tool.
integrity.visual_evidence: The GUI console log or a popup notification confirms the file was saved to the specific OpenBCI directory path.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply create a dummy file in the directory to simulate success.
integrity.visual_evidence: The trajectory shows the sequence of opening the menu and enabling the toggle before the screenshot action occurs.

privileged_info_for_vlm: OpenBCI GUI v5.2.2 features an 'Expert Mode' accessible via the Settings dropdown menu. When Expert Mode is enabled, the 'm' key functions as a shortcut to save a screenshot specifically to the '~/Documents/OpenBCI_GUI/Screenshots/' directory. The GUI typically displays a confirmation message in the console or as a toast notification when a screenshot is successfully captured via this shortcut.
